citation: kan a_2Mhi0EZlv, including Alex's answers of 2026-09-24; docs/mip/0002-muster-tabs.md, a Muster window
why: Every tab belongs to exactly one window, and this record is the only place that is written down: a daemon does not know which windows exist, and every window is a process of its own. What the cases pin is the record's own rules - one holder per tab, a closed window keeping its tabs, and which window takes a tab nobody holds - because every window acts on what it reads here, and two windows reading one record differently is two windows showing one tab.

cases.name: a window that has opened holds nothing until it takes a tab
cases.why: Opening is not a claim on anything. A window that took whatever it could see at open is the window from kan a_2Mhi0EZlv, which held nothing for an hour and a half and then drew the next tab anybody made.

cases.name: a tab belongs to the window that took it
cases.why: One holder per tab is the whole rule. The record says which window, and a window lists exactly the tabs that name it.

windows: window-1 pid=11 socket=/s/command-11.sock arrangement=/s/windows/window-1.toml focused=100 daemons=local
window-2 pid=22 socket=/s/command-22.sock arrangement=/s/windows/window-2.toml focused=200 daemons=local

cases.name: a tab moved to another window leaves the one that had it
cases.why: A tab is never in two windows, because herdr allows one client per terminal and a tab listed twice is one whose terminals the second window takes at the first click. So giving a tab to one window is taking it from the other, in one write.

windows: window-1 pid=11 socket=/s/command-11.sock arrangement=/s/windows/window-1.toml focused=100 daemons=local
window-2 pid=22 socket=/s/command-22.sock arrangement=/s/windows/window-2.toml focused=200 daemons=local

cases.name: a closed window keeps its tabs
cases.why: Its agents are still running on their daemons, and `muster window reopen` is supposed to bring the window back onto them. Letting go on close would hand them to whichever window is open, which is two windows' tabs in one list after a quit - the reopen failure measured on 0.7.0.

windows: window-1 pid=0 socket= arrangement=/s/windows/window-1.toml focused=100 daemons=local

cases.name: a window opening again keeps the tabs it held
cases.why: A window is its arrangement record, not its process (MIP-2), so a new pid is the same window coming back. Anything else would be a reopen that finds its tabs gone.

windows: window-1 pid=33 socket=/s/command-33.sock arrangement=/s/windows/window-1.toml focused=500 daemons=local

cases.name: a tab moved to a window that is not open waits for it
cases.why: `muster tab move --window window-3` names a closed window, and the tab goes there: it leaves this window now and is back when that one reopens. The record learns of the window from the move itself.

cases.name: a tab nobody holds joins the window that was most recently in front
cases.why: A tab made outside Muster - in herdr's own TUI, say - carries nothing that says where it belongs, and the window somebody was last looking at is where they will look for it.

windows: window-1 pid=11 socket=/s/command-11.sock arrangement=/s/windows/window-1.toml focused=100 daemons=local
window-2 pid=22 socket=/s/command-22.sock arrangement=/s/windows/window-2.toml focused=200 daemons=local

cases.name: a closed window takes nothing, however recently it was in front
cases.why: A tab given to a closed window is a tab nobody can see until that window is reopened, which may be never. Only open windows are asked.

windows: window-1 pid=11 socket=/s/command-11.sock arrangement=/s/windows/window-1.toml focused=100 daemons=local
window-2 pid=0 socket= arrangement=/s/windows/window-2.toml focused=200 daemons=local

cases.name: coming to the front makes a window the one a new tab joins
cases.why: Which window was in front last changes every time somebody clicks between them, so the record keeps the time each window came forward rather than an order fixed at open.

windows: window-1 pid=11 socket=/s/command-11.sock arrangement=/s/windows/window-1.toml focused=300 daemons=local
window-2 pid=22 socket=/s/command-22.sock arrangement=/s/windows/window-2.toml focused=200 daemons=local

cases.name: a tab nobody holds joins the window in front that follows its machine
cases.why: Only a window attached to a devenv hears that devenv's tabs. The window in front may not be one of them, and a window that cannot see a tab cannot show it - so it goes to the window most recently in front of the ones that can, rather than waiting on one that never will.

window-2 pid=22 socket=/s/command-22.sock arrangement=/s/windows/window-2.toml focused=200 daemons=local

cases.name: a window that attaches a machine can take its tabs
cases.why: Which machines a window follows changes when somebody attaches a devenv, and the record says so from then on.

window-2 pid=22 socket=/s/command-22.sock arrangement=/s/windows/window-2.toml focused=200 daemons=local

cases.name: a tab on a machine no open window follows is taken by nobody
cases.why: The next window to follow that machine takes it, the same way the next window to open takes a tab when none is open.

windows: window-1 pid=11 socket=/s/command-11.sock arrangement=/s/windows/window-1.toml focused=100 daemons=local

cases.name: with no window open, nobody takes a tab
cases.why: The next window to open takes it instead, which is also the upgrade path: the first window after this record existed is the only one open, and takes every tab the way a single window always did.

windows: window-1 pid=11 socket=/s/command-11.sock arrangement=/s/windows/window-1.toml focused=100 daemons=local

cases.name: a window waiting on a machine keeps that machine's new tab from the others
cases.why: Measured on 0.8.1 (kan a_2Mhi0EZlv): the daemon describes a new tab to every window before the one that asked hears the answer naming it. Without this, the window in front would take a tab another window asked for - which is the failure the card was raised for, arrived at by a different rule.

window-2 pid=22 socket=/s/command-22.sock arrangement=/s/windows/window-2.toml focused=200 daemons=local

cases.name: a window waiting on one machine does not hold up another
cases.why: What is expected is a tab on the machine the request went to. A tab on another machine at the same moment is somebody else's doing and joins the window in front as usual.

window-2 pid=22 socket=/s/command-22.sock arrangement=/s/windows/window-2.toml focused=200 daemons=devenv,local

cases.name: the answer arriving ends the wait
cases.why: The window that asked writes the tab it got and clears its expectation in the same write, and every other window hears the record move and decides again - so a tab made outside Muster in the meantime is only held up, not lost.

window-2 pid=22 socket=/s/command-22.sock arrangement=/s/windows/window-2.toml focused=200 daemons=local

cases.name: a closed window's wait is over
cases.why: A window that quit or crashed mid-request will never write the answer, so what it was waiting for joins an open window rather than waiting on it forever.

window-2 pid=22 socket=/s/command-22.sock arrangement=/s/windows/window-2.toml focused=200 daemons=local

cases.name: a wait lasts thirty seconds
cases.why: Far past any answer a daemon gives. An open window whose expectation is older than that lost the answer, and a tab should not wait on it forever.

window-2 pid=22 socket=/s/command-22.sock arrangement=/s/windows/window-2.toml focused=200 daemons=local

cases.name: closing ends a window's wait
cases.why: A window writes its own close, so it clears what it was waiting on then rather than leaving other windows to find out by dialing it.

window-2 pid=22 socket=/s/command-22.sock arrangement=/s/windows/window-2.toml focused=200 daemons=local

cases.name: a window that can never come back lets its tabs go
cases.why: A window whose arrangement is gone, pruned or never written, cannot be reopened, so a tab it held would be held by nobody who could ever show it. Forgotten, the tab joins an open window under the rule for a tab nobody holds.

cases.name: a tab whose name resolves nowhere is dropped
cases.why: Tab names are never reused, so a row for one that no longer exists is read by nothing ever again. Kept, the record would grow by a row for every tab anybody ever made.
